items.text: After a restart, each pane comes back on the shell it was opened on, in its folder.
Linux single-window mode keeps one window: every later window is a workspace that hands the one toplevel over.
The session agent's memory climb per closed pane is Debug allocator overhead, not a leak, and the Linux close-memory check now measures what the agent really keeps.
Panes in windows nobody is using draw at a capped rate: fifty busy cascaded windows go from ~11 cores to ~1.4.
